Cryptography

Valeur de sel

A random value added to data, typically passwords, before hashing to ensure that identical inputs produce different hash outputs, preventing precomputed attack vectors such as rainbow tables.

Questions and answers

What is Valeur de sel?

In this glossary, Valeur de sel refers to: A random value added to data, typically passwords, before hashing to ensure that identical inputs produce different hash outputs, preventing precomputed attack vectors such as rainbow tables.

How is Valeur de sel used in cybersecurity?

In cybersecurity communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "Les valeurs de sel sont utilisées dans le hachage des mots de passe pour empêcher les attaquants d'utiliser des tables arc-en-ciel pour inverser les hachages."

Definition

A random value added to data, typically passwords, before hashing to ensure that identical inputs produce different hash outputs, preventing precomputed attack vectors such as rainbow tables.

Operational example

Salt values are used in password hashing to prevent attackers from using rainbow tables to reverse hashes.
